title: GraphQL endpoint
summary: Introspection, suggestions, node(id:) BOLA, field/mutation authorization, batching, CSRF, and depth/cost.

checks.title: Introspection
checks.why: Production introspection or field suggestions disclose the schema the client never ships.
checks.validate: __schema or a typo suggestion returns fields the public contract does not list.

variants.name: Classic introspection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{__schema{types{name fields{name}}}}"}
variants.expect: Disabled in production, or limited to an allowlisted consumer. A full dump is a lead plus any hidden mutations.
variants.why: Introspection reveals the full schema; production should disable or restrict it.

variants.name: GET introspection
variants.payload:
GET /graphql?query=%7B__schema%7Btypes%7Bname%7D%7D%7D HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: Some stacks disable POST introspection and leave GET on.
variants.why: A GET query bypasses any method-based introspection gate.

variants.name: Field suggestion
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{user{emial}}"}
variants.expect: "Did you mean email?" confirms names even when introspection is off.
variants.why: Suggestions disclose field names even when introspection is blocked.

checks.title: Hidden mutations and fields
checks.why: A mutation or field exists that the public client never calls.
checks.validate: An undocumented operation executes or returns data.

variants.name: Common admin mutations
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"mutation { updateUserRole(id: 1, role: \"admin\") { id role } }"}
variants.expect: Try names from introspection / suggestions: deleteUser, impersonate, setRole, inviteAdmin.
variants.why: Mutation names follow conventions; probing common ones finds hidden admin operations.

variants.name: Typename probe
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{ __type(name: \"Mutation\") { fields { name } } }"}
variants.expect: Works when full __schema is off but __type is not.
variants.why: __typename leaks implementation type names across the schema.

groups.title: Authorization
groups.summary: node(id:), fields, mutations, and batches each need their own decision.

checks.title: node(id:) object authorization
checks.why: node(id:) and aliases skip the authorization the REST path has.
checks.validate: A node belonging to another account is returned.

variants.name: node(id:) swap
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{node(id:\"T3JkZXI6MTAwMg==\"){... on Order{id total}}}"}
variants.expect: Order 1002 is B's. Decode and recode other type prefixes too.
variants.why: Reading another object by global id is object-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Aliased parallel reads
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{a:order(id:1001){id} b:order(id:1002){id total}}"}
variants.expect: Each alias needs its own decision. b must not return B's order.
variants.why: Aliases let one query fetch many objects and compare which are authorised.

checks.title: Field-level authorization
checks.why: role, hashes, and PII fields are omitted by the default client query but still resolvable.
checks.validate: A field the matrix denies is returned.

variants.name: Sensitive field selection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{me{id email role passwordHash ssn taxId}}"}
variants.expect: role, hashes, and internal fields must be absent or unauthorized.
variants.why: Fields with per-field authorization can be read directly by selection.

variants.name: Nested owner fields
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{order(id:1002){id user{email role}}}"}
variants.expect: Even if the order is denied, a nested user leak is still a finding.
variants.why: Nested owner/tenant fields on an object expose data the object check does not cover.

checks.title: Mutation authorization
checks.why: A member can call an admin mutation or set a privileged input property.
checks.validate: A privileged write executes for a caller the matrix denies.

variants.name: Admin mutation as member
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"mutation { deleteUser(id: 42) { id } }"}
variants.expect: Must be unauthorized. Confirm the user still exists.
variants.why: A member invoking an admin mutation is function-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Input property mass-assign
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"mutation { updateMe(input: { role: \"admin\", verified: true }) { role verified } }"}
variants.expect: role/verified must be unchanged.
variants.why: Mutation inputs can include privilege fields the client should not set.

checks.title: Batched operations
checks.why: A batch mixes an allowed query with a denied one and the denied one still runs.
checks.validate: A denied operation in a batch returns data or changes state.

variants.name: JSON array batch
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

[{"query":"{me{id}}"},{"query":"{order(id:1002){id total}}"}]
variants.expect: Second element is B's order. Each member needs its own decision.
variants.why: Batched operations run against pooled rate/cost limits and can skip per-request checks.

variants.name: Alias flood / repeated fields
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{a1:me{id} a2:me{id} a3:me{id}}"}
variants.expect: Aliases must count toward cost. This is a lead for the depth/cost check, not a finding by itself.
variants.why: Aliases multiply work in one query, evading per-query cost limits.

checks.title: GraphQL CSRF
checks.why: A simple-request mutation (GET or form POST) runs in the victim browser.
checks.validate: A cross-origin simple request changes state.

variants.name: GET mutation
variants.payload:
GET /graphql?query=mutation%7BdeleteMe%7Bok%7D%7D HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Cookie: session=<victim>
variants.expect: Mutations over GET must be rejected.
variants.why: A mutation over GET can be triggered cross-site without a preflight.

variants.name: form-urlencoded mutation
variants.payload:
<form action="https://api.example.com/graphql" method="POST">
  <input name="query" value="mutation { deleteMe { ok } }">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit()</script>
variants.expect: Must fail without a custom content type + CSRF token / SameSite=Strict.
variants.why: A form-encoded POST is a CSRF-simple request that must still require a token.

checks.title: Depth and cost limits
checks.why: A nested or aliased query is expensive enough to be a cheap DoS.
checks.validate: A bounded expensive query is rejected. Do not actually DoS; one nested probe is enough.

variants.name: Deep nesting
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{me{friends{friends{friends{friends{id}}}}}}"}
variants.expect: Must 400 / cost-exceeded, not a multi-second 200. Stop after one demonstration.
variants.why: Deeply nested selections can exhaust the resolver regardless of cost limits.

variants.name: Wide connection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{users(first:10000){edges{node{id email}}}}"}
variants.expect: page size must be capped. Do not page through the corpus.
variants.why: A huge first/limit on a connection amplifies response cost.

checks.title: GraphQL baseline per transport
checks.why: Every later GraphQL test needs a known-good minimal operation per transport — the control for every mutation you send.
checks.validate: A minimal valid query recorded for each confirmed transport (POST, GET, persisted, multipart, websocket).

variants.name: Typename per transport
variants.payload: { __typename } over every confirmed transport (POST body, GET query, persisted-query id, multipart, subscriptions).
variants.expect: One recorded baseline per transport; refusals documented per transport too.
variants.why: The control comes first.

variants.name: Persisted-query shape
variants.payload: Capture a real persisted-query hash from the client; replay it as the baseline for that transport.
variants.expect: Hash resolves and executes; unknown hashes get a clear error (not a bypass).
variants.why: Persisted queries hide the query from logs — capture it now.

variants.name: Error-shape snapshot
variants.payload: Send one deliberately invalid query per transport; snapshot the error envelope.
variants.expect: Consistent error envelope recorded — later checks compare against it.
variants.why: Envelope changes reveal handler changes.

checks.title: Unauthorized mutation fields and inputs rejected
checks.why: Mutation inputs accept the full type by default — role, owner, and tenant fields ride inside "convenient" input objects.
checks.validate: Mutation inputs accept only permitted fields; unauthorized input fields are rejected, not ignored-and-applied.

variants.name: Privilege-field input
variants.payload: Include role/isAdmin/ownerId/tenantId in a mutation input type you can use.
variants.expect: Rejected with a field-level error; never silently applied.
variants.why: GraphQL makes mass assignment typed.

variants.name: Nested input smuggle
variants.payload: Nest the privilege field inside sub-inputs (user:{role:"admin"}).
variants.expect: Deep input validation reaches every level.
variants.why: Validators often stop at depth one.

variants.name: Mutation-for-read-type
variants.payload: Invoke mutations of privileged types that only read (adminViewer { users { email } }).
variants.expect: Field-level authorization on every type — naming is not policy.
variants.why: Reads behind mutations skip read guards.

checks.title: Query cost analysis on expensive combinations
checks.why: Nested, self-referential, and list-heavy queries cost exponential server work — a single request DoS.
checks.validate: Cost/depth analysis rejects or degrades expensive queries with a clear error at the documented limit.

variants.name: Depth bomb
variants.payload: A chain of nested list selections 5+ deep on harmless own data.
variants.expect: Rejected by depth/cost limits with a clear error.
variants.why: The classic single-request DoS shape.

variants.name: Cost probe
variants.payload: Repeat a moderately nested selection with growing breadth; find the refusal boundary.
variants.expect: Refusal at a documented cost; boundary stable (not timing-dependent).
variants.why: Find the wall, cite it.

variants.name: Introspection-driven heavy path
variants.payload: Use the schema to find the deepest relation path and build the minimal expensive query.
variants.expect: Same limits regardless of path; heuristics catch schema-guided shapes too.
variants.why: The schema is the attack map — limits must be path-independent.

checks.title: Aliases and repeats count toward limits
checks.why: Alias the same field a thousand times and every per-field limit is bypassed by name multiplication.
checks.validate: Aliases and repeated fields count toward depth/cost/complexity limits; per-operation totals cap repetition.

variants.name: Alias flood
variants.payload: One field aliased 50-100 times in a single query on your own object.
variants.expect: Rejected by operation-complexity limits — counted per alias.
variants.why: The oldest GraphQL limit bypass.

variants.name: Batched operations
variants.payload: Multiple operations in one request document; multiple queries in one array body.
variants.expect: Each operation counted; batching does not multiply the budget.
variants.why: Batching is aliasing at request scale.

variants.name: Fragment multiplication
variants.payload: Spread the same fragment many times in one operation.
variants.expect: Fragment spreads count toward complexity like inline fields.
variants.why: Fragments hide the repetition from naive counters.

checks.title: Pagination and connection traversal bounded
checks.why: first: 999999 and endless next-page walks are export and exhaustion primitives in one cursor.
checks.validate: Page sizes capped; cursor windows bounded; deep traversal limited per operation.

variants.name: Size inflation
variants.payload: first: 999999, last: 999999 on a connection you own.
variants.expect: Capped at the documented maximum with a clear error or truncation notice.
variants.why: The one-parameter export button.

variants.name: Cursor forging
variants.payload: Tamper with pagination cursors (decode, mutate offset/id, re-encode).
variants.expect: Forged cursors rejected or resolve within authorized bounds — never arbitrary seeks.
variants.why: Cursors are client input.

variants.name: Deep walk
variants.payload: Follow next-page automatically a bounded number of pages on your own data.
variants.expect: Traversal caps or rate-limits engage; total exposure bounded.
variants.why: Walk politely, measure the wall.

checks.title: Subscriptions authorized at subscribe and event time
checks.why: Subscriptions authorize at subscribe and then stream forever — permissions change, streams do not notice.
checks.validate: Each subscription checks caller authorization at subscribe AND per event dispatch; revocation ends streams.

variants.name: Foreign subscription
variants.payload: Subscribe to a topic rooted at another test account object.
variants.expect: Refused at subscribe — topic arguments are authorization inputs.
variants.why: Handshake auth is not topic auth.

variants.name: Event-time recheck
variants.payload: Subscribe to your own object; owner-assisted permission removal mid-stream; observe events.
variants.expect: Stream closes or events stop within the documented window.
variants.why: The stream that outlives its permission.

variants.name: Argument tampering mid-protocol
variants.payload: Change subscription variables (topic ids) over the same connection after connect.
variants.expect: Re-authorized per change; variable updates are new authorization decisions.
variants.why: WebSocket variable updates skip naive auth middleware.

checks.title: Errors without secrets or unauthorized data
checks.why: GraphQL errors love to include stack traces, query text, resolver paths, and partial data next to the error.
checks.validate: Error envelopes carry messages and paths only — no stacks, credentials, SQL, or data the query was not authorized for.

variants.name: Error envelope audit
variants.payload: Force type, auth, and resolver errors (harmlessly); inspect message, extensions, and any partial data field.
variants.expect: Clean envelopes; no stacks, internals, or leaked partial data.
variants.why: Every error type, one audit pass.

variants.name: Partial-data leak
variants.payload: Query a mix of authorized and unauthorized fields to force partial failure.
variants.expect: Errors for unauthorized fields WITHOUT data; no partial cross-account values.
variants.why: Partial success is where filters snap.

variants.name: Suggestions fuzz
variants.payload: Send slightly-wrong field names and inspect did-you-mean suggestions.
variants.expect: Suggestions limited to the caller's visible schema — not a private-type oracle.
variants.why: Helpful errors leak private schemas.

gql-node-swap.purpose: Reading another object by global id is object-level authorization failure.
gql-node-swap.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{node(id:\"T3JkZXI6MTAwMg==\"){... on Order{id total}}}"}
